    MA4704 · AEROELASTICITY

    Unsteady Aerodynamics

    #Review of Aerodynamics

    #Substantial Derivative

    Consider a fluid element moving through a flow field.

    V=ui+vj+wk

    Using chain rule of differentiation, acceleration is,

    a=DtDV​=∂t∂V​+∂x∂V​dtdx​+∂y∂V​dtdy​+∂z∂V​dtdz​

    a=(∂t∂​+∂x∂​dtdx​+∂y∂​dtdy​+∂z∂​dtdz​)V

    a=(∂t∂​+∂x∂​u+∂y∂​v+∂z∂​w)V

    💡

    a=(∂t∂​+V⋅∇)V

    where gradient operator ∇=∂x∂​i+∂y∂​j+∂z∂​k

    #Unsteady Bernoulli’s Equation

    Using Newton’s 2nd law,

    F=ma   →   A dP=(ρA dx)a   →   ρa=dxdP​

    For incompressible and inviscid unsteady flow,

    ρDtDV​=−∇P

    ρ(∂t∂​+V⋅∇)V=−∇P

    💡

    ρ∂t∂V​+ρ(V⋅∇)V=−∇P

    Assume irrotational flow such that curl V≡∇×V=0,

    0=∇×V

    0=(∂x∂​i+∂y∂​j+∂z∂​k)×(ui+vj+wk)

    0=(∂y∂w​−∂z∂v​)i+(∂z∂u​−∂x∂w​)j+(∂x∂v​−∂y∂u​)k

    ∴   ∂y∂w​=∂z∂v​,   ∂z∂u​=∂x∂w​,   ∂x∂v​=∂y∂u​

    With the above relations, it can be shown that,

    (V⋅∇)V

    =(u∂x∂​+v∂y∂​+w∂z∂​)(ui+vj+wk)

    =(u∂x∂u​+v∂y∂u​+w∂z∂u​)i+(u∂x∂v​+v∂y∂v​+w∂z∂v​)j+(u∂x∂w​+v∂y∂w​+w∂z∂w​)k

    =(u∂x∂u​+v∂x∂v​+w∂z∂u​)i+(u∂y∂u​+v∂y∂v​+w∂y∂w​)j+(u∂z∂u​+v∂z∂v​+w∂z∂w​)k

    =21​(∂x∂u2​+∂x∂v2​+∂z∂u2​)i+21​(∂y∂u2​+∂y∂v2​+∂y∂w2​)j+21​(∂z∂u2​+∂z∂v2​+∂z∂w2​)k

    =21​∂x∂​(u2+v2+w2)i+21​∂y∂​(u2+v2+w2)j+21​∂z∂​(u2+v2+w2)k

    =21​∇(u2+v2+w2)

    =21​∇(V⋅V)

    Unsteady Bernoulli’s equation,

    −∇P=ρ∂t∂V​+ρ[21​∇(V⋅V)]

    −∇P=∇(21​ρV⋅V)+ρ∂t∂V​

    −∇P=∇(21​ρ∇ϕ⋅∇ϕ)+ρ∂t∂​(∇ϕ)

    0=∇(21​ρ∇ϕ⋅∇ϕ)+∇(ρ∂t∂ϕ​)+∇P

    0=∇(21​ρ∇ϕ⋅∇ϕ+ρ∂t∂ϕ​+P)

    💡

    21​ρ∇ϕ⋅∇ϕ+ρ∂t∂ϕ​+P=Const.

    💡

    21​ρV1​2+ρ(∂t∂ϕ​)1​+P1​=21​ρV2​2+ρ(∂t∂ϕ​)2​+P2​

    where velocity potential ϕ=ϕ(x,y,z,t) such that ∂x∂ϕ​=u, ∂y∂ϕ​=v, ∂z∂ϕ​=w

    #Potential Flow — Sources & Vortices

    #Discrete & Distributive Sources

    For a discrete source of strength Λ,

    ϕ(x,y)=2πΛ​ln(r)

    ϕ(x,y)=2πΛ​ln(x−x1​)2+(y−y1​)2​

    ϕ(x,y)=4πΛ​ln[(x−x1​)2+(y−y1​)2]

    where (x1​,y1​) are the coordinates of the source,
    and     (x,y) are coordinates of the point of interest

    For distributive sources of strength λ,

    ϕs​(x,y)=2πλ ds​ln(r)

    ϕs​(x,y)=2πλ ds​ln(x−xs​)2+(y−ys​)2​

    Integrating to get total contribution of all the sources,

    ϕ(x,y)=∫S​ 4πλ​ln[(x−xs​)2+(y−ys​)2] ds

    #Discrete & Distributive Vortices

    For a discrete vortex of strength Γ,

    ϕ(x,y)=−2πΓ​tan−1(x−x1​y−y1​​)

    where (x1​,y1​) are the coordinates of the source,
    and     (x,y) are coordinates of the point of interest

    For distributive vortices of strength γ,

    ϕs​(x,y)=−2πγ ds​tan−1(x−xs​y−ys​​)

    Integrating to get total contribution of all the vortices,

    ϕ(x,y)=∫S​ −2πγ​tan−1(x−xs​y−ys​​) ds

    #Unsteady Aerodynamics

    Assumptions:

    • Angle of attack α(t) and heave h(t) are small in magnitude; no flow separation
    • Potential flow — incompressible ∇2ϕ=0 and irrotational ∇×∇ϕ=0
    • Kutta condition is satisfied such that ϕ(TE)=Finite
    • Circulation Γ remains constant over time

    Downwash velocity is influenced by freestream velocity U, α(t) and h(t).

    wU​(x,t)=−Usinα=−Uα

    wα˙​(x,t)=cosα−(x−a)α˙​=−(x−a)α˙

    wh˙​(x,t)=−h˙cosα=−h˙

    Downwash velocity is given by,

    w(x,t)=wU​+wα˙​+wh˙​

    w(x,t)=−Uα(t)−(x−a)α˙(t)−h˙(t)

    Velocity potential normal to surfaces must
    satisfy the following boundary conditions:

    1. ∂n∂ϕ​=w(x,t) Upper surface
    2. ∂n∂ϕ​=−w(x,t) Lower surface

    The velocity distribution of the airfoil can be replaced with a “source” sheet
    of strength λ(x,t)=w(x,t) on the upper surface Su​ and a “sink” sheet
    of strength λ(x,t)=−w(x,t) on the lower surface Sl​.

    #Complex Conformal Mapping

    An airfoil’s geometry is described by both x and y coordinates. To simplify the analysis, transform the airfoil’s complex shape into a simple geometry — a cylinder, such that ϕ
    can be derived from analyzing the fluid flow around the cylinder.

    Express downwash velocity as a complex variable, w=u+iv.
    Define a new complex variable for the cylinder, z=x+iy.

    The relationship between w and z is given by,

    💡

    w=z+zR2​

    Complex variable z can be rewritten as,

    z=Rcosθ+iRsinθ

    z=R(cosθ+isinθ)

    z=Reiθ

    Substituting into the relationship,

    w=z+zR2​

    w=Reiθ+ReiθR2​

    w=Reiθ+Re−iθ

    w=R(eiθ+e−iθ)

    w=R[(cosθ+isinθ)+(cosθ−isinθ)]

    w=2Rcosθ

    Comparing the coefficients for downwash velocity,

    w=2Rcosθ=u+iv

    u=2Rcosθ

    v=0

    As θ varies in the range 0≤θ<2π, point of interest shifts from
    the trailing edge when θ=0 to the leading edge when θ=π,
    and then back to the trailing edge when θ=2π.

    #Non-Circulatory Lift & Moment

    After performing conformal mapping, we get a cylindrical wing.
    Attach a “source” sheet on the upper section of the circle.
    Attach a “sink” sheet on the lower section of the circle.

    #Velocity Potential of Airfoil

    Velocity potential of a source at (x1​,y1​) is,

    ϕ(x,y)=4πλ​ln[(x−x1​)2+(y−y1​)2]

    Velocity potential of a sink at (x1​,−y1​) is,

    ϕ(x,y)=4π−λ​ln[(x−x1​)2+(y+y1​)2]

    Combined velocity potential of a pair of source and sink,

    ϕ(x,y)=4πλ​ln[(x−x1​)2+(y−y1​)2]+4π−λ​ln[(x−x1​)2+(y+y1​)2]

    ϕ(x,y)=4πλ​{ln[(x−x1​)2+(y−y1​)2]−ln[(x−x1​)2+(y+y1​)2]}

    ϕ(x,y)=4πλ​ln(x−x1​)2+(y+y1​)2(x−x1​)2+(y−y1​)2​

    Integrating to get the total contribution of all sources and sinks,

    ϕ(x,y,t)=4π1​∫−c/2c/2​ λln(x−x1​)2+(y+y1​)2(x−x1​)2+(y−y1​)2​ dx1​

    ϕ(x,y,t)=4π1​∫−c/2c/2​ 2w(x1​,t)ln(x−x1​)2+(y+y1​)2(x−x1​)2+(y−y1​)2​ dx1​

    ϕ(x,y,t)=2π1​∫−c/2c/2​ w(x1​,t)ln(x−x1​)2+(y+y1​)2(x−x1​)2+(y−y1​)2​ dx1​

    where w(x1​,t)=−Uα−(x1​−a)α˙−h˙

    Equation of a circle,

    x2+y2=R2=4c2​   →   y=4c2​−x2​

    x1​2+y1​2=R2=4c2​   →   y1​=4c2​−x1​2​

    Substituting the above into the velocity potential,

    ϕ(x,t)=2π1​∫−c/2c/2​ w(x1​,t)ln(x−x1​)2+(c2/4−x2​+c2/4−x1​2​)2(x−x1​)2+(c2/4−x2​−c2/4−x1​2​)2​

    ϕ(xˉ,t)=2πb​∫−11​ [−Uα−(bxˉ1​−a)α˙−h˙]ln(xˉ−xˉ1​)2+(1−xˉ2​+1−xˉ1​2​)(xˉ−xˉ1​)2+(1−xˉ2​−1−xˉ1​2​)​

    where b=2c​ and xˉ=bx​

    Performing the integration, we get the velocity potential for the upper and lower surfaces.

    💡

    ϕu​(xˉ,t)=b[Uα−aα˙+h˙]1−xˉ2​+21​b2α˙xˉ1−xˉ2​

    💡

    ϕl​(xˉ,t)=−ϕu​(xˉ,t)

    where b=2c​ and xˉ=bx​

    #Pressure Difference ΔP

    From unsteady Bernoulli’s equation,

    21​ρ∇ϕ⋅∇ϕ+ρ∂t∂ϕ​+P=Const.

    21​ρV2+ρ∂t∂ϕ​+P=Const.

    where V= local air velocity and P= local static pressure

    Local air velocity V is the sum of freestream velocity U along the x-axis and the
    contribution of the distribution sources and sinks with velocity potential ϕ(xˉ,t).

    V=Ucosα+∂x∂ϕ​=U+∂x∂ϕ​

    Local static pressure on the upper and lower surfaces are,

    Pu​=−21​ρ(U+∂x∂ϕu​​)2−ρ∂t∂ϕu​​+Const.

    Pl​=−21​ρ(U−∂x∂ϕu​​)2+ρ∂t∂ϕu​​+Const.

    Note that ϕu​(xˉ,t)=−ϕl​(xˉ,t).

    Pressure difference between the upper and lower surface is,

    💡

    ΔP=Pl​−Pu​=2ρ(U∂x∂ϕu​​+∂t∂ϕu​​)=2ρ(bU​∂xˉ∂ϕu​​+∂t∂ϕu​​)

    where xˉ=bx​

    #Non-Circulatory Lift

    Non-circulatory lift per unit span,

    Lnc​=∫−bb​ ΔP dx=b∫−11​ ΔP dxˉ

    Lnc​=2ρb∫−11​ bU​∂xˉ∂ϕu​​+∂t∂ϕu​​ dxˉ

    Lnc​={2ρU∫−11​ ∂xˉ∂ϕu​​ dxˉ}+{2ρb∫−11​ ∂t∂ϕu​​ dxˉ}

    Lnc​={2ρU[ϕu​(1,t)−ϕi​(−1,t)]}+{2ρb∫−11​ ∂t∂ϕu​​ dxˉ}

    Note that velocity potential ϕu​(1,t)=0 and ϕu​(−1,t)=0.

    Non-circulatory lift per unit span simplifies to,

    Lnc​=2ρb∫−11​ ∂t∂ϕu​​ dxˉ

    Lnc​=2ρb∫−11​ b[Uα˙−aα¨+h¨]1−xˉ2​+21​b2α¨xˉ1−xˉ2​ dxˉ

    Lnc​={2ρb2(Uα˙−aα¨+h¨)∫−11​ 1−xˉ2​ dxˉ}+{ρb3α¨∫−11​ xˉ1−xˉ2​ dxˉ}

    Lnc​={2ρb2(Uα˙−aα¨+h¨)2π​}+{ρb3α¨(0)}

    💡

    Lnc​=ρπb2(Uα˙−aα¨+h¨)

    Non-circulatory lift is generated due to acceleration h¨ in the heave-DOF,
    angular acceleration     α¨ in the pitch-DOF, and Coriolis acceleration Uα˙.

    #Non-Circulatory Moment

    Non-circulatory moment per unit span (clockwise +ve),

    Mnc​=−∫−bb​ ΔP(x−a) dx

    Mnc​=−∫−bb​ 2ρ(bU​∂xˉ∂ϕu​​+∂t∂ϕu​​)(x−a) dx

    Mnc​=−2ρb2∫−11​ (bU​∂xˉ∂ϕu​​+∂t∂ϕu​​)(xˉ−ba​) dxˉ

    💡

    Mnc​=ρπb2[ah¨+Uh˙+U2a−(a2+8b2​)α¨−4c​Uα˙]

    Note that non-circulatory moment is derived with respect to the elastic axis.

    #Circulatory Lift & Moment

    In reality, it is known that is circulation around an airfoil.
    This circulation will generate additional lift and moment.

    #Velocity Potential of Wake Vortices

    As wake vortices travel downstream, circulation is generated around the airfoil.
    The magnitude of circulation is determined by imposing the Kutta condition.

    Consider a pair of discrete vortices located at (X0​,0) and (b2/X0​,0).

    Velocity potential induced by this pair of vortices at any arbitrary point is,

    ϕΔΓ​=2πΔΓ​(tan−1x−X0​y​−tan−1x−b2/X0​y​)

    ϕΔΓ​=2πΔΓ​(tan−1xˉ−Xˉ0​yˉ​​−tan−1xˉ−1/Xˉ0​yˉ​​)

    💡

    ϕΔΓ​=−2πΔΓ​tan−11−xˉxˉ0​1−xˉ2​xˉ0​2−1​​

    where xˉ=bx​ and xˉ0​=2Xˉ0​+1/Xˉ0​​ and Xˉ0​=bX0​​

    #Pressure Difference ΔP

    From derivation of non-circulatory forces,

    ΔP=2ρ(U∂x∂ϕΔΓ​​+∂t∂ϕΔΓ​​)

    ΔP=2ρ(bU​∂xˉ∂ϕΔΓ​​+∂xˉ0​∂ϕΔΓ​​∂t∂xˉ0​​)

    ΔP=2ρ(bU​∂xˉ∂ϕΔΓ​​+∂xˉ0​∂ϕΔΓ​​bU​)

    ΔP=b2ρU​(∂xˉ∂ϕΔΓ​​+∂xˉ0​∂ϕΔΓ​​)

    💡

    ΔP=bπρU(ΔΓ)​1−xˉ2​xˉ0​2−1​xˉ+xˉ0​​

    where xˉ=bx​

    #Circulatory Lift & Moment

    Elemental circulatory lift per unit span over the wing,

    ΔLc​=∫−bb​ ΔP(xˉ,xˉ0​) dx

    ΔLc​=b∫−11​ ΔP(xˉ,xˉ0​) dxˉ

    ΔLc​=b∫−11​ bπρU(ΔΓ)​1−xˉ2​xˉ0​2−1​xˉ+xˉ0​​ dxˉ

    ΔLc​=ρU(ΔΓ)xˉ0​2−1​xˉ0​​

    Circulatory lift per unit span over the wake vortex,

    Lc​=∫1+∞​ ΔLc​(xˉ0​)

    Lc​=ρU∫1+∞​ ΔΓxˉ0​2−1​xˉ0​​

    Lc​=ρU∫1+∞​ (bγ dxˉ0​)xˉ0​2−1​xˉ0​​

    💡

    Lc​=ρbU∫1+∞​ γxˉ0​2−1​xˉ0​​ dxˉ0​

    Note that γ is still unknown and circulatory lift cannot be evaluated yet.

    Circulatory moment about the flexural axis,

    💡

    Mc​=−ρbU∫1+∞​ γ[2b​xˉ0​−1xˉ0​+1​​−22a+b​xˉ0​2−1​xˉ0​​] dx0​

    Note that γ is still unknown and circulatory moment cannot be evaluated yet.

    Vortex strength γ can be determined by imposing the Kutta condition, which states
    that the “local velocity of the trailing edge must be finite” whereby ∂x∂ϕtot​​=finite.

    Total velocity potential ϕtot​ caused by both sources and vortices.

    From derivation of non-circulatory forces, velocity potential due to sources is,

    ϕ1​(xˉ,t)=b[Uα−aα˙+h˙]1−xˉ2​+21​b2α˙xˉ1−xˉ2​

    From derivation of circulatory forces, velocity potential due to vortices is,

    ϕΔΓ​=−2πΔΓ​tan−11−xˉxˉ0​1−xˉ2​xˉ0​2−1​​

    ϕΔΓ​=−2πbγ dxˉ0​​tan−11−xˉxˉ0​1−xˉ2​xˉ0​2−1​​

    ϕ2​(xˉ,t)=−2πb​∫1+∞​ γ(tan−11−xˉxˉ0​1−xˉ2​xˉ0​2−1​​) dxˉ0​

    Total velocity potential is the sum of the respective potentials.

    ϕtot​=ϕ1​(xˉ,t)+ϕ2​(xˉ,t)

    ∂xˉ∂ϕtot​​=1−xˉ2​b​{−(Uα−aα˙+h˙)xˉ+21​bα˙(1−2xˉ2)+2π1​∫1+∞​ γxˉ−xˉ0​xˉ0​2−1​​ dxˉ0​}

    At the trailing edge where xˉ=1, the denominator 1−xˉ2​=0.
    To satisfy the Kutta condition, the numerator must be equal to zero.

    0=−(Uα−aα˙+h˙)xˉ+21​bα˙(1−2xˉ2)+2π1​∫1+∞​ γxˉ−xˉ0​xˉ0​2−1​​ dxˉ0​

    0=−(Uα−aα˙+h˙)−21​bα˙+2π1​∫1+∞​ γ1−xˉ0​xˉ0​2−1​​ dxˉ0​

    0=−2π[Uα+h˙−(a−2b​)α˙]+∫1+∞​ γ1−xˉ0​xˉ0​2−1​​ dxˉ0​

    ∫1+∞​ γ1−xˉ0​xˉ0​2−1​​ dxˉ0​=2π[Uα+h˙−(a−2b​)α˙]

    ∫1+∞​ γ1−xˉ0​xˉ0​2−1​​ dxˉ0​=2πQ

    Define a new variable called the Theodorsen function.

    💡

    C≡∫1+∞​ γxˉ0​−1​xˉ0​+1​​ dxˉ0​∫1+∞​ γxˉ0​2−1​xˉ0​​ dxˉ0​​

    Circulatory lift and moment (per unit span) can be rewritten as,

    💡

    Lc​=2πρbUCQ

    💡

    Mc​=−ρπbU[b−(2a+b)C]Q

    #Theodorsen Function

    For an airfoil with a prescribed slow pitching and heaving harmonic motion,
    its variation in vorticity γ can be described by a sinusoidal graph (sine wave).

    Vorticity can be expressed as,

    γ(xˉ0​,t)=γ0​ei(ωt+kxˉ0​)

    where reduced frequency k=Uωb​

    Substituting into the Theodorsen function,

    C≡∫1+∞​ γxˉ0​−1​xˉ0​+1​​ dxˉ0​∫1+∞​ γxˉ0​2−1​xˉ0​​ dxˉ0​​≡∫1+∞​ xˉ0​−1​xˉ0​+1​​eikxˉ0​ dxˉ0​∫1+∞​ xˉ0​2−1​xˉ0​​eikxˉ0​ dxˉ0​​

    💡

    C(k)=1−1−(0.0455/k)i0.165​−1−(0.3/k)i0.335​

    where reduced frequency k=Uωb​

    • Re part — magnitude drop in circulatory lift/moment due to harmonic motion of airfoil
    • Img part — phase lag in circulatory lift and moment in relation to motion of airfoil
    • At k=0, the airfoil is not oscillating → no magnitude drop such that ∣C(0)∣=1
    • As k increases, magnitude drops to 21​, maximum lift is 21​ that of quasi-steady lift
    • Quasi-steady — assume steady conditions for a flow that is actually unsteady
    • Unsteadiness is corrected using the Theodorsen function C

    When an airfoil moves very slowly (quasi-steady):

    • Oscillation frequency ω≈0
    • Reduced frequency k≈0
    • Magnitude ∣C(0)∣=1
    • Phase lag ∠C(0)=0°

    #Aeroelastic Equations of Motion

    Consider a flat airfoil with its elastic axis A located distance a from the mid-chord.

    Summation of vertical forces ↓+ve,

    ∑F=maO​

    −L−kh=m(h¨−aα¨)

    Lift + Linear spring force = Mass × Acceleration

    Summation of moments about O clockwise +ve,

    ∑MO​=IO​α¨

    M−kT​α−La−kha=IO​α¨

    M−kT​α+m(h¨−aα¨)a=IO​α¨

    Moment + Torsional spring force + Moments due to linear forces

    Writing the EoM in matrix form,

    [m−ma​−maIA​​]{h¨α¨​}+[k0​0kT​​]{hα​}={−LM​}

    where IA​=IO​+ma2

    Assume airfoil motion is a sinusoidal motion.

    h=h0​sin(ωt)=h0​eiωt   →   h¨=−ω2h0​sin(ωt)=−ω2h0​eiωt

    α=α0​sin(ωt)=α0​eiωt   →   α¨=−ω2α0​sin(ωt)=−ω2α0​eiωt

    Substituting into the EoM,

    💡

    [−ω2m+kmaω2​maω2−ω2IA​+kT​​]{h0​α0​​}eiωt={−LM​}

    Total lift, which is the sum of non-circulatory and circulatory components,

    L=Lnc​+Lc​

    L=ρπb2(Uα˙−aα¨+h¨)        +2πρbUC[Uα+h˙−(a−2b​)α˙]

    L={ρπb2[U(iω)α0​+aω2α0​−ω2h0​]           +2πρbUC[Uα0​+iωh0​−iωα0​(a−2b​)]}eiωt

    Total moment, which is the sum of non-circulatory and circulatory components,

    M=Mnc​+Mc​

    M=ρπb2[ah¨+Uh˙+U2a−(a2+8b2​)α¨−4c​Uα˙]          −ρπbU[b−(2a+b)C][Uα+h˙−(a−2b​)α˙]

    M={ρπb2[−aω2h0​+U(iω)h0​+U2α0​+ω2α0​(a2+8b2​)−4c​U(iω)α0​]             −ρπbU[b−(2a+b)C][Uα0​+iωh0​−iωα0​(a−2b​)]}eiωt

    Substituting the total lift and moment equations into the EoM,

    💡

    [A11​A21​​A12​A22​​]{h0​α0​​}={00​}

    A11​=k−ω2−ω2ρπb2+2(iω)ρπbUC

    A12​=maω2+(iω)ρπb2U+ω2ρπab2+2ρπbU2C−2(iω)ρπbUC(a−2b​)

    A21​=maω2+ω2ρπab2−(iω)ρπb2U+(iω)ρπbU[b−(2a+b)C]

    A22​=kT​−ω2IA​−ρπab2U2−ω2ρπb2(a2+8b2​)+(iω)ρπb2U4c​           +ρπbU2[b−(2a+b)C]−(iω)ρπbU[b−(2a+b)C](a−2b​)

    Critical flutter condition can be predicted by equating the determinant to zero.

    💡

    D(ωF​,UF​)=det​A11​A21​​A12​A22​​​=0

    where ωF​= flutter frequency and UF​= flutter airspeed
